outcomes: Each Rush project is a Putnami project with an edge to each Rush project its package.json depends on, in the mode the workspace adopted
In delegate mode, putnami build, test and lint run rush on each affected project, and Rush's build cache decides what reruns
In import mode, each Rush project is a TypeScript project that Putnami's runner, installer and cache serve, and a target whose tool @putnami/typescript does not run keeps running with rushx
nonGoals: Installing or switching a Rush version: the toolchain check compares and never installs
Rewriting rush.json or command-line.json, or a project's package.json beyond the exports an import adds (D-066); an import never rewrites a script
Rush subspaces, version policies and publishing: rush publish and rush version keep running through Rush
A Rush repository whose rush.json is not at the Putnami workspace root

text: In delegate mode, the probe answers each rush.json project: its folder, its packageName as source name and the name rush receives, the projects the observe Rush detector says it depends on, attributed build-graph, extension @putnami/rush, tag rush, the workspace root as stack root.
In import mode, the default, it answers a project whose putnami.json names @putnami/rush as such, and every other rush.json project as bare, with no extension and no source name.
A directory rush.json does not list is no project.

The sync task writes in each project's putnami.json the extension of the mode, the mode param or else the recorded mode, import by default, an unknown one failing, and the project IDs it depends on, and removes the other mode's extension.
In delegate mode it adds rush.json, command-line.json and the Rush lockfile as filePatterns, disables test and lint without a Rush command of that name, and retracts a former project;
in import mode it disables a task with no script.
It rewrites a file only on a change.

requirements.text: In import mode as in delegate mode, putnami validate compares each project's putnami.json with rush.json and the project manifests, writes nothing, and fails with rush.sync_stale when a sync would change one.

text: Each task compares the version the banner of rush --help states with the rushVersion of rush.json, then runs at the workspace root rush build --to <package>, which builds the projects upstream of it too, or rush test or rush lint --only <package>, which runs on that project alone.
Each task depends only on its project's graph step, which runs no rush.
Putnami's cache is off for every task, and the result records delegatedTo rush.
A failing step fails with stacks.step_failed.
The test task reads the JUnit and coverage files a project names in its putnami.json, under options.@putnami/rush.tasks.test.reports, into the test and coverage summary.
A project that names none passes or fails on the exit code alone, and the sync lists those projects.

requirements.text: In delegate mode, when common/config/rush/build-cache.json is missing or does not set buildCacheEnabled to true, the sync warns once that each delegated build reruns the projects upstream of its own.

text: The sync writes nothing it cannot map.
It lists, with the reason, each command-line.json bulk or phased command other than build, test and lint, and in import mode each project script other than build, test and lint;
those keep running through Rush.

requirements.text: The manifest passes the stack core's conformance kit: its markers are the profile's, it lists the rush:build, rush:test and rush:lint selectors, each command runs the graph step, which depends on the graph step upstream, then its task, which depends on its own graph step alone, and every task, the graph task included, sets cache.enabled to false.

text: In import mode, a build, test or lint script moves to @putnami/typescript only when that extension runs its tool: bun build or tsc alone, bun test, Vitest or Jest with no argument that picks a configuration or a subset, Biome or a bare ESLint, with no command chained.

Any other script keeps running with rushx <task> in the project's directory: its putnami.json names @putnami/rush beside @putnami/typescript, disables each task for the extension that does not run it, and the sync lists the script (D-070).

In import mode, the sync adds exports {".": "./src/index.ts"} after the top-level main or types of a package.json whose build script runs bun build, that declares no exports, names a file outside src/ there, holds src/index.ts and that rush.json does not publish, and writes a tsconfig.json extending the root's where a project holds no tsconfig*.json.
It keeps every other byte, warns about each file it writes and each manifest it cannot edit, and a dry sync shows each diff.
In import mode, a script that moves to @putnami/typescript does what it did: a test script moves with options["@putnami/typescript:test"].types false, since the script type-checked nothing.
A bun build script moves only when Putnami's Bun build writes the entries the package.json names: none outside src/, or entries D-066 rewrites; otherwise it stays on Rush and the sync says why.
When a lint moves, the sync says that putnami lint --impacted lints the projects a change touches, not their dependents.
